correctness.rationale: The 3-by-4 Vandermonde kernel and multiplicity-vector bound restrict all nontrivial triple collisions to one unbalanced or one balanced relation. Affine normal forms and a size-two stabilizer prove incidence counts for all characteristic>=7 fields. Orthogonality gives H=s^3+6s e2+12e3 plus the single 12Re(c_a^3 conj(c_bc_cc_d)) cross term. Outer-arm symmetric inequalities force equal moduli, and the derivative is -36r(r^4+r^3+6r^2-3r-7)/(r^2+3)^4. Descartes gives exactly one positive root and hence global maximality and phase equality. An independent standard-library checker passed exhaustive geometry p=7,11,13,17 and 28 Fourier/convolution comparisons.

value.rationale: The four-site finite-field parabola is the smallest natural step beyond known three-parabolic-mode sixth-moment results. Its complete and counted additive-collision classification explains why sharp sixth-power norms jump from 4 only in special arithmetic configurations. The unbalanced sharp value 4.203233399... and all complex extremizers provide a natural exact Lambda(6) invariant over every prime-power field of characteristic>=7, with a cube-root field-existence threshold.
